BiblicalUsage: Ebronah was one of the camps of Israel in the wilderness, the stop just before Ezion-geber on the way to the Red Sea. The journey list in Numbers names it twice, once for arriving and once for leaving, and then the people moved on. Its name means passage, which fits a camp that was only a place to pass through.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God led His people one camp at a time, and even the stops we barely remember were part of His route. Ebronah reminds me that the journey matters even when the stay is short.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
